newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks extend gains at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks extend gains at close.

text.p: Argentina's bolsa battled profit-takers and stretched a week-long rally at the close Thursday, driven by the Dow's surge past 7000 and a strong quarterly profit for bellwether YPF, dealers said.

"The market was firm but subdued in the first half of the session as players took some profits. But it recovered its momentum when the Dow pierced 7000 and the U.S. long bond yield tumbled (to 6.63 percent from 6.7 percent)," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers.
The blue-chip MerVal index advanced 0.8 percent to 724.47, boosting gains so far this week to three percent.
"The market will probably reach its near-term target of 730 tomorrow or Monday but then it could level out as investors square positions ahead of next Friday's options expirations," said Bonanno.
After a long climb the MerVal stalled at 728 on February 16, 1994. If it tops that mark it would set a five-year high.

"The trend is unmistakably bullish and underpinned by news like today's strong fourth-quarter YPF profit," another trader said. "The results reflect the fact the economy is gaining steam and justifying the bolsa's steady advance over the past two months."
Floor volume remained heavy at 36 million pesos compared to 37.9 million Wednesday, while over-the-counter turnover swelled to 168 million pesos from 133 million Wednesday.
The broad market index tacked on 0.7 percent, with winners outpacing losers 36 to 23 and 21 issues closing flat.
Top MerVal performers were textile firm Alpargatas, power company Central Costanera and food giant Molinos, which jumped 4.7 percent, 2.4 percent and 2.2 percent respectively.
sharpest losers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa, down 2.2 percent, and carmakers Sevel and Ciadea, both off 1.9 percent.
